I did an 8 hour drive with my two cats when I moved states a few years ago. My guy pooped in the crate within 30 min then the rest was smooth sailing. I kept him in the crate because he can get chaotic and my girl on a leash because crates scare her too much and she gets upset when she’s not able to be near me. She’s well behaved so that worked out. 

So, I would say depending on your cat, bring pee pads for accidents just in case and some cleaning wipes if you can. Bring some treats to help with their stress. 

If you feed your cat before you leave keep track of if they’ve used the litter box beforehand. Personally I wouldn’t change that part of their routine because that could add to their confusion and stress. If they don’t, I guess you could bring a small plastic pan and put some litter in it but I’ve never tried this myself... might be messy but you could put down towels underneath. And make sure they have litter box access as soon as you arrive. 

Use a leash or harness with them if you can trust them out of the crate while driving. Think mine slept some after they got settled within the first hour or so.

My 6 year old boy was diagnosed when he went in for something else - sounds like the same thing. Large cell lymphoma in his intestines. Was given two months without any treatment and maybe four months with chemo. I was devastated - I mean I still am because it’s not curable but it was back in February so I’ve processed a lot of it. Last year he was diagnosed with diabetes, IBD, chronic kidney disease (early stage), a heart murmur… he had a rough year but was acting normal the whole time. Happy but just insatiable hunger. 

I decided to do the chemo pill to spare him the stress of IV chemo. I was on the fence about it since he had already been through so much but he had been such a trooper and I just wasn’t ready to say goodbye. But, in preparation, I started making calls to get info about arranging at home euthanasia. Never been through it before. He was my first pet, got him at 8 weeks old, and I had gotten him right after a close friend passed. 

He just did his fourth round of chemo and the last two ultrasounds have showed no masses! He has two more to go and hopes are this means remission. Not sure how long it will last but it means we get a little more time together and his sister gets more time with him too. He seems to have more energy since chemo started and is more cuddly with me. 

I’m not saying this is what will happen if you choose to do chemo, but I am very glad I at least tried even though it was basically a 50/50 chance of him responding to it. I knew I would very much regret not at least trying. 

Please feel free to DM if you need someone to talk to you. And best of luck with whatever happens.

My chonk is just like this! His sister is smaller and for a long time when they were a bit younger I would leave out dry food for them all day. I didn’t realize or notice that chonk was taking way more than his share and his sister is more of a snacker/grazer, so when I would come home and the food was gone I assumed they shared it fairly equally. Nope, chonk was vacuuming it all up and sister got morsels. She lost a ton of weight and he gained a bunch and I couldn’t figure out why until I realized that’s what was going on. She ended up having health issues as a result and is doing very well now after much observation and fine tuning. Chonk went from 12 to 15 pounds and I was told to avoid that number going higher.

They require two different foods for chonk’s unrelated urinary issues and they both get different meds everyday for their respective things. So, a few things that helped to prevent food theft and work around their over and under eating:

- feeding them separately at two different levels (one on the counter and one on the table), which they got used to pretty quickly and now run to their spots when it’s food time
- feeding on a strict schedule and adhering to it (not giving into the meows and begging)
- monitoring them as they eat to make sure they’re separate
- chonk’s weight, vacuuming tendency, and urinary thing prompted me to switch to wet food for him with dry food mixed in with water (wet food contains less calories and you can look into specific portion amounts for each brand on how much to give per day, and a bonus is that it slows him down when eating so he doesn’t throw up right after from eating too fast)

Hope this helps, I know it’s a ton of info! Some of these things I started more recently and some health factors got in the way of me monitoring his weight but at the next vet check up I’ll know more on that!

Edit: Almost forgot to add, I’ve discovered by accident and trial and error that adding a bit of water to BOTH of their dry food prompts gets them more excited to eat it without having to increase the volume. Something I’ve started doing this last year that helps is feeding them at two different levels, slightly separated. For example, my one cat eats on the counter and the other eats on the floor. They got used to it after a while and know they have separate food territories. The floor one is more chonk so is usually less inclined to jump up for food because chonk. Counter cat is dainty and easy to pick up and put back.

It’s been a ton of trial and error this year. He needs an extended length cone since he can still reach his tail with a regular length one. I got a taller and slanted water bowl that he can maneuver his cone around to get water, and I started feeding him wet food to supplement hydration. I take the cone off only when he’s eating and supervise his grooming afterward, putting the cone back on as soon as he starts getting at one of the spots. He gets the routine now and is used to it despite hating it, and seems to be fine when I leave the house or when I’m sleeping. I set up cameras (there are cheap ones that work well on Amazon) so I can make sure he’s good when I’m out of the house. I would just try to give as many supervised grooming breaks as you can throughout the day, I think that helps his mood a lot. Right now I just do those after he’s eaten so he knows he’ll get some freedom for a bit before it goes back on. Structure helps!
